test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-II (Statistics) Official Paper-II (Held On: 19 Jan, 2025)
subject: general
question: Data sets with high kurtosis:
solution:
**The correct answer is : tend to have heavy outliers **

__**Explanation:**__

 
• Kurtosis measures the "tailedness" of a distribution.
 
• High kurtosis (leptokurtic) indicates that the distribution has heavy tails, meaning more data points lie far from the mean.
 
• This results in more extreme values (outliers) compared to a normal distribution.
 
• Symmetry is not guaranteed, and high kurtosis does not mean no outliers.

 So, datasets with high kurtosis tend to have heavy outliers.
